subject: [Urgent] Finco EU gateway timeouts — customer P1 / exec attention
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: support@finco.com
Date: 2027-05-19T07:12:00Z
Subject: Realtime: elevated 502/503 for finco-eu edge pool

Heads up — our EU edge pool serving Finco is showing a ~12% 502/503 rate starting ~07:05 UTC. Latency has doubled for short requests and we're seeing a retry amplification pattern from the customer's SDK (client retries every 150ms up to 10 attempts). I've attached short metrics export and top-line logs.

Immediate ask: can we confirm if this is load balancing (proxy) or backend inference runtime? Logs show an increase in 502s at the reverse-proxy layer with 502 responses including "upstream reset" and "connect timeout".

Attachments: redwood_eu_lb_metrics_20270519.csv, redwood_server_logs_20270519.txt

—Sean
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: John Miller <john.miller@finco.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finco.com
Date: 2027-05-19T07:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Realtime: elevated 502/503 for finco-eu edge pool

Thanks for the heads up. This is impacting checkout flows for our EU customers — traffic dropped by ~30% and several merchants are reporting failed charges. Our engineers see the same 502s and the SDK is already ramping retries. Can you share an ETA? We need a mitigation path (eg: rollback to earlier edge config, route to alternate region, or short-term rate-limiting).

John Miller
Head of Infrastructure, Finco Payments
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: John Miller <john.miller@finco.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-19T07:29:00Z
Subject: Re: Realtime: elevated 502/503 for finco-eu edge pool

John — I'm escalating to execs and the Platform incident channel. Apologies for the customer impact. Quick summary of actions we are taking now: 

- Sean: confirm whether this is proxy-level connection churn (NGINX/h2) vs. inference runtime saturation.
- Marissa: coordinate with Finco on short-term routing (can they failover to eu-west-2?) and capture any SDK/client changes that increased concurrency.
- I'll request immediate throttling rules and enable the standby regional pool if needed.

I will escalate for SLA credits if the impact meets threshold; please keep me posted on merchant impact so we can scope. I'll get back within 20 minutes with a concrete mitigation.

Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | rachel.kim@redwood.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: NOC Team <noc@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T07:41:00Z
Subject: Internal: quick findings — EU proxy connection resets

Short update: preliminary trace shows surge of short-lived TCP connections hitting one of the EU load balancer frontends. Upstream pool for finco-eu-backend-3 is returning "connection reset by peer" and then the proxy returns 502. No OOMs on the inference hosts; CPU and memory look normal.

Hypothesis: a recent Finco SDK change increased concurrent short-lived sessions which interacts poorly with our keepalive/proxy tuning — causing upstream sockets to be closed while the proxy still tries to dispatch. This amplifies when the client aggressively retries, resulting in retry storm -> queue saturation -> 502/503.

Immediate mitigations I propose (ordered):
1) Apply short-term 50% rate-limit on Finco origin at the edge (throttle new connections) — low friction, quick roll.
2) Failover traffic for a subset of merchants to standby eu-west-2 pool (canary 10% -> 50%).
3) Adjust proxy keepalive_timeout to reduce premature resets; low-risk but needs rollout.

I'll push the LB throttles now and report metrics in 10 minutes.

—Sean
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: John Miller <john.miller@finco.com>, ops@finco.com, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, legal@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-19T08:03:00Z
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Finco EU gateway timeouts — customer P1 / exec attention

John — we just applied conservative connection throttles at the EU edge and started a 10% canary failover of traffic to an isolated standby pool. Early signal: 502 rate dropped from 12% -> 6% in canary slices; overall region rate down to ~8% and latency improving for short requests.

Next steps:
- We'll expand the failover to 40% over 30 minutes if metrics continue to improve.
- We recommend Finco temporarily increase client-side backoff (200ms -> 500ms) while we complete the fallback; this will reduce retry amplification.
- Post-incident, we'll propose a tuning plan (keepalive, proxy buffer settings) and a recommended SDK concurrency limit.

I realize this is high impact — I'll schedule an exec brief and a postmortem once stabilized. For now, confirm if Finco wants us to proceed with the 40% failover immediately.

Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: John Miller <john.miller@finco.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finco.com
Date: 2027-05-19T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Finco EU gateway timeouts — customer P1 / exec attention

Thanks — the canary improvements are visible on our side and merchants are reporting fewer failures. Please proceed with the 40% expansion and publish a short status update to affected merchant support queues. We'll push a quick SDK update to increase backoff and throttle concurrent sessions where possible.

Also please include our CTO on the exec brief (cto@finco.com). We will want a postmortem with timeline and recommended resiliency steps.

—John
